meta.title: Where AI shops: ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and more
meta.description: How each AI assistant finds, compares and buys products, what merchants need for each one, and what ecentic does there today.

index.title: Where AI shops.
index.description: Each assistant finds, compares and buys products in its own way. Here’s what each one needs, and what ecentic does there today.

method.title: How we check this
method.body: We read each platform’s own documentation and announcements. Every page shows the date we last checked it and links to its sources. “Simulated” means ecentic runs product comparisons with that model; it does not mean a direct shopping-channel connection.
method.note: This directory focuses on assistants with a documented commerce route or a simulation available in ecentic.

meta.title: Selling through Google AI Mode and Gemini
meta.description: How Google’s AI Mode and Gemini choose and buy products, what Merchant Center needs, and what ecentic does for Google’s AI today.

google.title: Selling through Google AI Mode and Gemini
google.description: Google’s AI answers shopping questions using merchant product data. For select merchants, shoppers can check out through Google.

sections.title: How this assistant shops
sections.description: Google’s shopping experiences use Merchant Center catalog data. Universal Cart launched in the US on 15 October 2026, with options to continue to a merchant’s cart or use Google Pay where checkout is enabled. The merchant remains the seller of record.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.description: Merchant Center product data, including the offer’s price, availability and checkout eligibility. Accurate product pages and clear shipping and return information are part of keeping that offer ready.

sections.title: How merchants get in
sections.description: Google lists native checkout for select merchants with eligible products in the US, Canada and Australia. Its Merchant Center integration hub is rolling out in the US first; Canada and Australia are expected early next year. Merchants must complete Google’s technical validation and approval steps.

sections.title: What ecentic does here today
sections.description: These labels describe ecentic features. Platform eligibility is a separate step.

sections.title: What’s next
sections.description: Upcoming integrations have no promised launch date. Register your interest to help us prioritize.

capabilities.simulate: Gemini compares selected products with named competitors in ecentic’s store scans.
capabilities.fix: Publish listing changes to Shopify or WooCommerce. Shopify stores can separately send published changes to Merchant Center.
capabilities.checkout: WooCommerce plugin endpoints and a checkout playground are live. Shopify stores can audit Merchant Center checkout settings. Google program admission remains your step.
capabilities.track: Recognizes Gemini referrals and supported Google AI agent traffic on connected Shopify stores.

faqs.question: Do we need Merchant Center for Google’s checkout?
faqs.answer: Yes. The documented merchant route runs through Merchant Center. Your account, products and checkout integration must meet Google’s eligibility requirements.

faqs.question: Can ecentic join Google’s checkout program for us?
faqs.answer: No. ecentic helps prepare and test data and settings. The application, validation and approval remain between your business and Google.

faqs.question: Does Merchant Center sync work on WooCommerce?
faqs.answer: Not yet. ecentic’s Merchant Center connection is available for Shopify stores today.

google.trademark: Google AI Mode and Gemini are trademarks of Google LLC. ecentic isn’t affiliated with or endorsed by Google LLC.

meta.title: Selling through ChatGPT shopping
meta.description: How ChatGPT recommends products, what merchant feeds contain, how approved checkout integrations work, and what ecentic does today.

chatgpt.title: Selling through ChatGPT
chatgpt.description: ChatGPT uses merchant product data to recommend products. Shoppers can follow links to your store; approved app integrations can offer checkout inside ChatGPT.

sections.title: How this assistant shops
sections.description: OpenAI’s commerce documentation describes structured product feeds for product discovery. Its current beta checkout documentation also supports approved partners opening a checkout experience through a connected plugin. Availability depends on the merchant’s approved integration.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.description: Product and variant records with titles, descriptions, images, URLs, prices and availability. OpenAI’s guidance also covers accurate seller identity, shipping and returns. Setting a checkout eligibility flag does not itself enable checkout.

sections.title: How merchants get in
sections.description: Apply through OpenAI’s merchant onboarding route. Product feed access is for approved partners, with schema validation and an agreed delivery method. A ChatGPT checkout app requires its own integration and approval; a feed alone does not provide it.

sections.title: What ecentic does here today
sections.description: These labels describe ecentic features. Platform eligibility is a separate step.

sections.title: What’s next
sections.description: Upcoming integrations have no promised launch date. Register your interest to help us prioritize.

capabilities.simulate: ChatGPT evaluates selected products against competitors in store scans.
capabilities.fix: Listing checks include OpenAI feed rules. Publish a revised title and description, or structured data through its separate action, to a connected store.
capabilities.checkout: The ecentic ChatGPT app is coming soon; its directory publication has not been confirmed. Current checkout tools do not establish a live ChatGPT app integration.
capabilities.track: Tracks ChatGPT referrals and recognized agent visits on Shopify.

faqs.question: Can shoppers buy inside ChatGPT?
faqs.answer: OpenAI’s current beta documentation describes checkout inside ChatGPT for approved plugin integrations. Other product links take shoppers to the merchant. Eligibility depends on the integration; publication of ecentic’s app has not been confirmed.

faqs.question: We use Shopify. Does ecentic enroll our store in ChatGPT?
faqs.answer: No. Channel eligibility and any catalog distribution by your commerce platform are separate from ecentic. We test product comparisons and help improve the listing data you control.

faqs.question: How can a merchant send product data to OpenAI?
faqs.answer: Apply through OpenAI’s merchant onboarding route. Approved partners can provide a product feed that meets its specification. ecentic checks listing quality today; our dedicated ChatGPT feed export is coming soon.

chatgpt.trademark: ChatGPT is a trademark of OpenAI. ecentic isn’t affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI.

meta.title: How Claude recommends products
meta.description: How retailers can build commerce agents with Claude, and how ecentic tests Claude’s product choices and improves listing data.

claude.title: Selling through Claude
claude.description: Test how Claude compares your products. Anthropic’s documented commerce route lets retailers build agents using their own catalog and checkout.

sections.title: How this assistant shops
sections.description: Anthropic’s commerce guide describes agents that search a retailer’s catalog, compare products and work with its cart and checkout. These are merchant-built experiences, whose behavior depends on the tools and data the retailer supplies.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.description: The retailer provides catalog, inventory, policy and cart tools to its own agent. ecentic’s simulations use the product and competitor information assembled for the comparison; they are not a live ranking report from Claude.

sections.title: How merchants get in
sections.description: Anthropic publishes a blueprint for building a commerce agent. It is a development route for your own experience, not evidence that connecting to ecentic enrolls your store in a Claude shopping directory.

sections.title: What ecentic does here today
sections.description: These labels describe ecentic features. Platform eligibility is a separate step.

sections.title: What’s next
sections.description: There is no dedicated Claude checkout connector on our announced build list. You can use the live simulations and listing workflow today.

capabilities.simulate: Claude compares selected products with named competitors in store scans.
capabilities.fix: The same title, description and separate structured-data publish actions are available for connected Shopify and WooCommerce stores.
capabilities.checkout: ecentic has no dedicated Claude checkout connection today.
capabilities.track: Recognizes Claude referrals and supported agent traffic on Shopify.

faqs.question: Can Claude buy from our store?
faqs.answer: A retailer can build a Claude-powered agent with catalog, cart and checkout tools. That does not mean ecentic currently connects your store to a consumer Claude checkout; we do not.

faqs.question: Why simulate Claude?
faqs.answer: A controlled comparison helps you see which product facts influence Claude’s choices. The results apply to that simulation setup and can differ from another assistant or a real shopping session.

faqs.question: Do the fixes only help Claude?
faqs.answer: The changes are to the product information on your own store. Other readers can use that clearer data too, but no recommendation or sales outcome is guaranteed.

claude.trademark: Claude is a trademark of Anthropic PBC. ecentic isn’t affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic PBC.

meta.title: Selling through Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Checkout
meta.description: How Copilot Checkout works, who can join, and what ecentic is building for Microsoft Merchant Center.

copilot.title: Selling through Microsoft Copilot
copilot.description: Copilot recommends products and, through Copilot Checkout, lets eligible US shoppers buy in the conversation.

sections.title: How this assistant shops
sections.description: Microsoft describes product discovery and checkout on copilot.com and in the Copilot mobile app. The merchant remains the seller of record and uses its own fulfillment and customer relationship.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.description: Product data from the web and merchant feeds. The Microsoft Merchant Center route requires product records with the additional checkout attributes described in Microsoft’s onboarding guide.

sections.title: How merchants get in
sections.description: Microsoft’s current eligibility is English-language merchants selling to US buyers in USD. Its documented routes include Microsoft Merchant Center, automatic Shopify enrollment and Stripe Agentic Commerce Suite. A feed setup step is still a pilot for selected merchants.

sections.title: What ecentic does here today
sections.description: These labels describe ecentic features. Platform eligibility is a separate step.

sections.title: What’s next
sections.description: Upcoming integrations have no promised launch date. Register your interest to help us prioritize.

capabilities.simulate: Copilot is not in ecentic’s store scan panel.
capabilities.fix: A Microsoft Merchant Center feed export is on the build list. There is no live ecentic feed connection today.
capabilities.checkout: Checkout attributes for the planned Microsoft feed are coming soon. Microsoft’s program requirements will still apply.
capabilities.track: Tracks Copilot referrals on connected Shopify stores.

faqs.question: How do we join Copilot Checkout?
faqs.answer: Follow Microsoft’s current onboarding route through Microsoft Merchant Center, Shopify or Stripe. English-language merchants serving US buyers in USD are eligible; some setup remains limited to selected merchants.

faqs.question: Does ecentic support Copilot today?
faqs.answer: ecentic tracks Copilot referrals on Shopify. Copilot simulations and a direct feed connection are not live. The Microsoft Merchant Center feed is on our build list.

faqs.question: Will the feed guarantee checkout approval?
faqs.answer: No. Microsoft controls admission and technical requirements. The planned ecentic export will prepare data; it cannot promise approval or recommendations.

copilot.trademark: Microsoft Copilot is a trademark of Microsoft Corporation. ecentic isn’t affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft Corporation.

meta.title: Selling through Perplexity shopping
meta.description: How Perplexity presents shopping results, where its merchant program is documented, and what ecentic supports today.

perplexity.title: Selling through Perplexity
perplexity.description: Perplexity answers shopping questions with product cards. ecentic tracks its referrals on Shopify; store scans and a merchant feed are coming soon.

sections.title: How this assistant shops
sections.description: Perplexity’s shopping announcement describes product cards and a Buy with Pro experience for eligible products in the US. Where that purchase option is unavailable, shoppers follow a link to the merchant’s website.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.description: Product information from merchants and shopping results. Perplexity describes integrations with merchant websites and a merchant program intended to make price and product details more complete.

sections.title: How merchants get in
sections.description: Perplexity’s official shopping announcement links to its free merchant program for large retailers. Follow the official program link for current eligibility. We have not verified a broader enrollment route or a live ecentic catalog connection.

sections.title: What ecentic does here today
sections.description: These labels describe ecentic features. Platform eligibility is a separate step.

sections.title: What’s next
sections.description: Upcoming integrations have no promised launch date. Register your interest to help us prioritize.

capabilities.simulate: Adding Perplexity to store scans is on the build list. It is not one of the three current store-scan models.
capabilities.fix: A dedicated Perplexity merchant feed is coming soon. Store listing changes remain available through Shopify and WooCommerce.
capabilities.checkout: ecentic has no dedicated Perplexity checkout connection today.
capabilities.track: Tracks Perplexity referrals and recognized agent traffic on Shopify.

faqs.question: How do merchants join?
faqs.answer: Start with the merchant program linked in Perplexity’s official shopping announcement. That source describes a free program for large retailers; confirm current access with Perplexity.

faqs.question: Does ecentic support Perplexity today?
faqs.answer: We track its referrals on Shopify stores. Adding Perplexity to store scans and building a merchant feed are coming soon.

faqs.question: Does a simulation prove a product will appear in Perplexity?
faqs.answer: No. A model comparison is separate from a live product recommendation, feed acceptance or checkout eligibility.

perplexity.trademark: Perplexity is a trademark of Perplexity AI, Inc. ecentic isn’t affiliated with or endorsed by Perplexity AI, Inc.

meta.title: Selling through Amazon’s AI: Shop Direct and Alexa
meta.description: How Shop Direct brings products from merchant websites to Amazon search and Alexa for Shopping, and what ecentic is building.

amazon.title: Selling through Amazon’s AI
amazon.description: Shop Direct can bring products from your own site into Amazon’s shopping experience. Eligible Buy for Me purchases are completed on the merchant’s website.

sections.title: How this assistant shops
sections.description: Amazon introduced Alexa for Shopping on 13 May 2026, bringing together Rufus and Alexa+. Shop Direct surfaces products from external merchant websites in Amazon search and its shopping assistant. Shoppers can visit the merchant; eligible offers also support Buy for Me.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.description: Catalog information supplied by the merchant through a solution provider or Amazon’s Selling Partner API. The merchant verifies its website and manages participation through the Shop Direct Merchant Workspace.

sections.title: How merchants get in
sections.description: Amazon launched the free Merchant Workspace on 4 November 2026. Shop Direct is available to US customers and accepts eligible merchant websites, including merchants that also sell on Amazon. Registration, website verification and catalog sharing are required.

sections.title: What ecentic does here today
sections.description: These labels describe ecentic features. Platform eligibility is a separate step.

sections.title: What’s next
sections.description: Upcoming integrations have no promised launch date. Register your interest to help us prioritize.

capabilities.simulate: Amazon’s shopping assistant is not in ecentic’s scan panel.
capabilities.fix: Sending an optimized catalog to Shop Direct is on the build list, subject to the required application approval.
capabilities.checkout: There is no live ecentic connection to Buy for Me.
capabilities.track: ecentic does not provide a dedicated Amazon Shop Direct traffic integration today.

faqs.question: Do we need an Amazon marketplace store?
faqs.answer: No. Shop Direct features products from merchants’ own websites. Amazon describes participation as free and the shopping experience as available to US customers.

faqs.question: Does ecentic connect to Shop Direct today?
faqs.answer: Not yet. A Shop Direct catalog connection is on our build list and will require the relevant Amazon application approval. Register your interest below.

faqs.question: Where does the shopper buy?
faqs.answer: Shop Direct can send the shopper to the merchant’s website. For eligible Buy for Me offers, Amazon’s agent completes the purchase on that website.

amazon.trademark: Amazon and Alexa are trademarks of Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates. ecentic isn’t affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon.
